jobs.title: Open Application
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Why this posting exists

We don't have a perfectly titled role waiting for you here, and that's exactly the point.

Some of the best people we've worked with didn't fit a job description when we met them. They were builders, operators, and problem-solvers who showed up, got how we think, and found (or created) the place where they could do their best work. This posting is for them. It's for you.

If you're drawn to what we're building at Plug and you can see yourself thriving in an early-stage, high-ownership environment, we want to be connected even if the title doesn't exist yet.

About Plug

Plug is an online marketplace built exclusively for electric vehicles, where consumers, dealers, and commercial partners trade in, sell, and auction used EVs. Consumers can get an instant cash offer in minutes, backed by data-driven pricing and battery state-of-health analysis, with end-to-end pickup, payment, and title transfer. Plug liquidates every vehicle it acquires through a competitive wholesale auction, where franchise and independent dealers across the United States bid in real time on inventory sourced directly from consumers, dealers, and commercial partners. The result is a single platform that gives sellers a fast, fair exit and gives dealers a dedicated channel for sourcing used EV inventory. Founded in 2023 and led by former Tesla executives, Plug has facilitated nearly $100M in EV sales since launch and is backed by a $20M Series A from Lightspeed Venture Partners. Plug is building the AI-native transaction rails behind the used EV market's exponential growth. Visit plugmotors.com to learn more.

Who we're looking for

We care far more about how you operate than the exact box your résumé fits in. The people who do well here tend to:

  • Own outcomes, not tasks. You see what needs to happen and move, without waiting for permission or a perfect spec.

  • Move fast and stay honest. You'd rather ship, learn, and adjust than polish something in private for a month. When you're wrong, you say so quickly.

  • Get your hands dirty. No job is beneath you. Early-stage means the founder, the lead, and the newest hire might all be doing the unglamorous work side by side.

  • Think from first principles. You question the default, but you do the homework before you do — you're not contrarian for its own sake.

  • Raise the bar around you. People do their best work near you, and you make the team better than the sum of its parts.

  • Operate well in ambiguity. Missing context doesn't paralyze you; you make a reasonable call, flag your assumptions, and keep moving.

We're function-agnostic on this posting: engineering, operations, go-to-market, product, design, finance, people, whatever your edge is. If the traits above sound like you, the function will sort itself out in conversation.

How we work

We're a startup, and we mean it. Small team, big surface area, real stakes. You'll have an unusual amount of influence and a correspondingly unusual amount of responsibility. We default to trust, direct feedback, and a fast pace, and we protect the people doing the work with real benefits and a culture that doesn't confuse "intense" with "careless."

What to include in your application

Help us see the person, not just the bullet points:

  • A short note on why Plug. What about what we're building pulls at you.

  • A quick line on where you think you'd add the most value, and why.

  • Anything that shows your work - a project you owned end to end, something you built, shipped, or fixed. Links welcome.

  • A résumé is fine, but we'll read the note first.

What to expect next

We read every open application. If there's a fit — now or as we grow — we'll reach out to start a conversation. Even when the timing isn't right, strong applicants often hear from us later when the right opening appears. We try to respect your time and be clear about where things stand.

Job Title: IT Manager
Team: Administration/IT
Location: Onsite - Sawtelle (Between Santa Monica & West LA)
Employment Type: Full-time, Salary, Exempt
Reports To: VP, Finance

About Plug
Plug is the marketplace for used electric vehicles. Consumers get an instant cash offer backed by battery-health data, and dealers across the US bid in real time on that inventory. Former Tesla executives founded Plug in 2023. We’ve facilitated over $150M in EV sales and raised a $20M Series A led by Lightspeed Venture Partners.

Why Plug

  • You’ll own a piece of the biggest infrastructure opportunity in automotive.

  • You’ll work on a platform built exclusively for EVs, with nothing adapted from legacy automotive.

  • You’ll be part of an AI-native company. We’re rethinking how work gets done at a fundamental level.

  • You’ll work directly with operators who have scaled multi-billion dollar businesses in automotive, EV, and marketplaces.

  • You’ll have real ownership, high autonomy, and a direct line to company outcomes.

The Role
We’re about 40 people and growing, and we need someone to own IT end to end. You’ll keep our people productive and our systems secure: getting new hires set up on day one, removing access the day someone leaves, and turning how we run IT into clear, written processes. As a fintech company, our banking and lending partners hold us to a high security bar, and you’ll help us meet it.

What You’ll Do

  • Provide first-line support for IT issues across the company.

  • Run onboarding and offboarding with HR. Laptops, accounts, and app access are ready on day one. Revoke accounts and collect equipment on the last day.

  • Administer Google Workspace and Rippling, including user accounts, groups, app provisioning, and device management.

  • Set and enforce security controls: MFA and SSO, device encryption and updates, password management, and least-privilege access.

  • Audit accounts, access, licenses, and permissions on a set schedule. Remove what’s no longer used.

  • Write and maintain the IT SOPs. Follow them consistently.

  • Manage IT vendors and SaaS tools. Track usage, renewals, and spend.

  • Answer security questionnaires and audits from our banking and lending partners.

  • Manage laptop and equipment inventory, plus conference room and AV equipment.

What You’ll Bring

Minimum Qualifications

  • 3+ years in IT support or systems administration.

  • You’ve owned IT as the primary person responsible for a company’s IT, with or without a team.

  • Hands-on Google Workspace administration: user accounts, groups, and app provisioning.

  • Hands-on experience with MFA and SSO. You’ve set them up, enforced them, or managed access through them.

  • Working knowledge of endpoint management and access control.

  • Hands-on support for macOS and Windows.

  • Examples of IT processes or SOPs you’ve written and maintained.

Nice to Have

  • Experience with Rippling or a similar HRIS or device management platform.

  • Startup or small-company experience.

  • Scripting or automation for repetitive IT work, such as onboarding, offboarding, or access reviews.

  • Networking basics and conference room AV experience.

  • Experience with SOC 2 or a similar security audit.

Not sure you should apply? Do it.
Research consistently shows that people from under-represented groups are more likely to talk themselves out of applying if they don’t meet 100% of the listed requirements. You don’t need to check every box. If this role excites you and you bring most of what’s listed under “What You’ll Bring,” we want to hear from you.

Compensation and Benefits
Annual salary: $105,000 to $120,000

Salary ranges come from independent, third-party benchmarking against national compensation data. Where an offer falls within the range depends on relevant experience, specialized skills, training and qualifications, current business needs, and market conditions. We review ranges periodically and may adjust them as the market changes.

Benefits & Perks

  • Health, Vision, and Dental insurance

  • 401(k) plan

  • Equity

  • Unlimited PTO

  • Daily lunch and dinner stipend, plus a fully stocked kitchen

  • Dog-friendly office and on-site EV charging

  • 30-day remote work from anywhere policy

  • Ongoing opportunities for growth and development

This full-time position is in-person, based in Sawtelle (between Santa Monica and West Los Angeles). We will not provide relocation assistance to successful candidates. We do not offer sponsorship at this time.

Acknowledgments
Plug is an equal opportunity employer. We don’t discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, creed, national origin, ancestry, sex, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, pregnancy, age, marital status, military or veteran status, physical or mental disability, medical condition, genetic information, or any other characteristic protected by law. Plug will consider qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records in accordance with the Los Angeles Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring and the California Fair Chance Act.

Job Title: Sr. Reconditioning Technician
Team: Business Operations
Location: Onsite - Norwalk, CA
Employment Type: Full-time, Hourly, Non-Exempt
Reports To: General Manager

About Plug
Plug is the marketplace for used electric vehicles. Consumers get an instant cash offer backed by battery-health data, and dealers across the US bid in real time on that inventory. Former Tesla executives founded Plug in 2023. We’ve facilitated over $150M in EV sales and raised a $20M Series A led by Lightspeed Venture Partners.

Why Plug

  • You’ll own a piece of the biggest infrastructure opportunity in automotive.

  • You’ll work on a platform built exclusively for EVs, with nothing adapted from legacy automotive.

  • You’ll be part of an AI-native company. We’re rethinking how work gets done at a fundamental level.

  • You’ll work directly with operators who have scaled multi-billion dollar businesses in automotive, EV, and marketplaces.

  • You’ll have real ownership, high autonomy, and a direct line to company outcomes.

The Opportunity
As Plug’s first Reconditioning Technician, you’ll help develop and scale a brand-new function that challenges how reconditioning is done in the automotive industry today. You’ll own the entire reconditioning process from start to finish: inspecting, repairing, and ensuring all cars meet Plug’s “Retail Ready” standard. On day one, you will also manage vendor relationships, create SOPs, and provide input on relevant system development efforts. Soon after, you will start building a team of junior technician(s) and/or operations specialist(s).

You’ll report directly to Plug’s General Manager and have direct influence over how this function is built from the ground up and how it rolls out to other locations across the country.

What You’ll Do

Inspect and Recondition Vehicles

  • Conduct thorough inspections (diagnostics, exterior, interior, mechanical, and road test) on all incoming vehicles.

  • Perform light reconditioning (e.g., tires, brake pads, cabin air filters, wiper blades, etc.) and non-powertrain repairs (e.g., exterior trim, door handles, suspension, etc.).

  • Diagnose, identify, and resolve complex issues across all major vehicle systems using various diagnostic software and tools.

  • As the team expands: mentor and develop junior technicians, provide day-to-day guidance, and sign off on repairs.

Build a Scalable Operation

  • Track inventory and order replacement parts from OEMs and third-party distributors. Develop a sourcing strategy to keep parts needed for common repairs in stock.

  • Direct end-to-end vehicle movement from intake to repair to prep and pickup.

  • Monitor battery state-of-charge levels and keep them above the defined threshold for all vehicles on-site.

  • Coordinate repairs with on-site (mobile) and off-site service vendors.

  • Create Plug’s in-house reconditioning SOPs from the ground up and continuously update them with improvements discovered as the operation scales.

  • Maintain a clean, safe, and organized workspace.

Serve as Plug’s Reconditioning Subject Matter Expert

  • Support implementing remote diagnostics in the cash offer process.

  • Serve as Plug’s in-house subject matter expert on reconditioning and technical vehicle issues to support products and programs across the company.

What You’ll Bring

  • 3+ years of automotive technician experience, with hands-on diagnostic work required.

  • Previous EV OEM experience (e.g., Tesla, Rivian, Lucid) strongly preferred. Powertrain (HV battery and drive unit) experience is a plus.

  • Strong diagnostic instincts and experience with OEM and aftermarket software and scan tools.

  • Ability to read wiring diagrams, service manuals, and technical knowledge bases.

  • Experience owning a wide scope of work across various skill sets, from hands-on diagnostics, inspections, and repair to on-site operations and SOP development, until we expand the team.

  • Comfortable working independently in an environment where you define your team’s processes from the ground up.

  • Naturally curious, with a willingness to experiment with different ways to continuously improve and meet our aggressive turnaround-time goals.

  • ASE certifications strongly preferred: A-series (A4-A8) plus L1 and/or L3 advanced, and L4 (ADAS).

  • Valid driver’s license with a clean record.

Physical Requirements

  • Stand and walk for extended periods.

  • Lift up to 50 pounds.

  • Bend, kneel, squat, and work underneath vehicles.

  • Operate lifts, power tools, and diagnostic equipment.

  • Comfortable working indoors and outdoors around moving vehicles and shop equipment.

  • Safely drive and road-test vehicles.

You don’t need to check every box. If this role excites you and you bring most of what’s listed under “What You’ll Bring,” we want to hear from you.

Compensation and Benefits
Hourly Wage: $45 to $60

Wage ranges come from independent, third-party benchmarking against national compensation data. Where an offer falls within the range depends on relevant experience, specialized skills, training and qualifications, current business needs, and market conditions. We review ranges periodically and may adjust them as the market changes.

Job Title: Full-Stack Software Engineer
Team: Engineering
Location: Onsite - Sawtelle (Between Santa Monica & West LA)
Employment Type: Full-time, Salary, Exempt
Reports To: Engineering Lead

About Plug
Plug is the marketplace for used electric vehicles. Consumers get an instant cash offer backed by battery-health data, and dealers across the US bid in real time on that inventory. Former Tesla executives founded Plug in 2023. We’ve facilitated over $150M in EV sales and raised a $20M Series A led by Lightspeed Venture Partners.

Why Plug

  • You’ll own a piece of the biggest infrastructure opportunity in automotive.

  • You’ll work on a platform built exclusively for EVs, with nothing adapted from legacy automotive.

  • You’ll work directly with operators who have scaled multi-billion dollar businesses in automotive, EV, and marketplaces.

  • You’ll have real ownership, high autonomy, and a direct line to company outcomes.

The Opportunity
We are looking for a Full-Stack Software Engineer to join our growing team. You’ll report to our engineering lead and own features and components within our products, working closely with senior software engineers (SSEs) on scope, architecture, and cross-system tradeoffs. We’re building systems like AI-powered pricing intelligence, real-time connectivity to vehicle manufacturer APIs, auction applications, and data pipelines that aggregate EV-specific information from dozens of sources, all to make the wholesale EV market faster, smarter, and more transparent.

As a member of the team, you’ll help build the technical and product foundation for our growing business, with direct mentorship from senior engineers as you grow into more ownership. We’re building a culture that cares about collaboration, encourages intellectual honesty, celebrates technical excellence, and is driven by careful attention to detail and planning for the future. We believe diverse perspectives and experiences are key to building great technology and a thriving team. Sounds cool? Let’s work together.

What You’ll Do

  • Collaborate with colleagues and contribute your voice in product design sessions, architecture discussions, and code reviews.

  • Design, implement, test, debug, and document work on new and existing software features, ensuring they meet business, quality, and operational needs.

  • Take ownership of features, with support from SSEs on architecture or cross-system trade-offs, understand the ultimate goal, and evaluate effort and priority in an agile environment.

  • Use agentic coding tools to write clear, efficient, maintainable code, and grow your judgment on flexibility and scalability with guidance from senior engineers.

  • Contribute to team productivity and process improvements.

About Plug
Plug is the marketplace for used electric vehicles. Consumers get an instant cash offer backed by battery-health data, and dealers across the US bid in real time on that inventory. Why Plug

  • You’ll own a piece of the biggest infrastructure opportunity in automotive.

  • You’ll work on a platform built exclusively for EVs, with nothing adapted from legacy automotive.

  • You’ll be part of an AI-native company. We’re rethinking how work gets done at a fundamental level.

  • You’ll work directly with operators who have scaled multi-billion dollar businesses in automotive, EV, and marketplaces.

  • You’ll have real ownership, high autonomy, and a direct line to company outcomes.

Why This Role
Partnerships are how Plug scales supply and demand at the same time. The Partnerships team owns the relationships that power Plug’s auction: consumer marketplaces, dealer groups, and commercial vehicle sellers, such as fleets, rental companies, OEMs, and other high-volume consignors.

Reporting to the Head of Partnerships, you will own a major slice of that portfolio end to end. You are not running a support function, and you are not waiting for direction. You set the plan for your accounts, drive it across Operations, Sales, Product, and Finance, and answer for the results.

Your Mission
Our company mission is to electrify the used car industry. Your job is to turn Plug’s most important partnerships into durable, growing programs and be the person inside the company who makes them work.

How We Think About Partnerships
Partnerships are a business, not a relationship-management exercise. Every program should answer at least one of: does this increase vehicle supply, increase dealer demand, improve transaction speed, improve margin, or strengthen Plug’s position with a partner? We don't confuse activity with progress, and we don't keep programs alive out of politeness.

What You Will Own

  • Own a portfolio of strategic partnerships: Carry direct accountability for a defined set of partner relationships and the numbers they produce. Set the objectives for your accounts inside the team’s goals, build the plan, and drive it without needing it handed to you.

  • Grow the programs you own: Find the expansion inside existing relationships, such as new lanes, new vehicle types, and new commercial structures, and build the case for it. Bring the analysis, not just the idea.

  • Lead cross-functionally without authority: Get Operations, Sales, Product, Engineering, and Finance aligned on what your partners need and when. You will not own those teams, so influence, clarity, and credibility are the job.

  • Maintain excellence throughout the relationship: Own onboarding, implementation, and the ongoing operating cadence. Track commitments and milestones, resolve issues end to end rather than escalating them, and surface risk before it lands.

  • Be the partner’s advocate and Plug’s filter: Translate partner needs into clear internal priorities and product requirements with enough detail that other teams can act. Push back internally when a partner is right, and push back on the partner when Plug is.

  • Build the playbook: Document how Plug runs strategic partnerships so the approach scales past you, and contribute the standards and methods the next hires will run on.

  • Bring AI-native solutions to your work: We want people who don’t just execute the process but rebuild it, and who apply new tools to their own workflow before asking for headcount.

Success After 12 Months

  • Measurable growth in vehicle supply from the partnerships you own.

  • Program revenue from your portfolio growing against plan.

  • At least one existing program materially expanded in scope or commercial value.

  • Partner commitments and program milestones consistently met, with risk flagged early.

  • Cross-functional teams moving on your partner priorities without escalation.

  • Reporting and forecasts on your portfolio the exec team trusts without checking.

  • A documented partnership playbook a new hire could run.

What You’ll Bring

  • 5+ years of relevant experience in partnerships, business development, account management, or commercial roles, with real ownership of outcomes rather than support of someone else’s.

  • A track record of growing existing relationships into larger programs, with numbers you can speak to.

  • Proven ability to lead cross-functional work without authority and drive decisions.

  • Strong executive presence and clear written communication with both partners and internal teams.

Preferred Experience

  • Automotive, fleet, OEM, or marketplace experience, strongly preferred but not required.

  • Experience with two-sided or supply-constrained businesses where partnerships drove liquidity.

  • Experience structuring commercial terms alongside legal and finance.

  • Already using AI tools in your daily workflow to move faster.

How We Operate
We hire builders who value ownership, velocity, curiosity, and measurable outcomes. We move quickly, make data-driven decisions, and embrace AI as a core operating principle. We hire for skill set over background, and people advance here because their impact grows, not because of tenure or headcount.

The people who do well here scope their own work, run their own process, and keep multiple workstreams moving without close management. They are comfortable with complexity and ambiguity, and can take a partly defined problem and come back with a plan. High agency, low ego, and a bias for action. You put yourself in front of people, and you own the outcome.

What Makes This Role Unique
You will own relationships that directly determine how fast the company grows, with the autonomy to run them like your own business and direct exposure to how a two-sided EV marketplace gets built. This seat offers a clear path to broader commercial ownership as Plug scales.

  • Automotive, EV, or marketplace experience is a plus, not required.
